why does my face get flaky every winter?

Flakes around the nose and brows that come back every winter often have a name: seborrheic dermatitis. A 2024 review of 1.26 million people put it at about 4 in 100.

In one hospital's records of 5,316 patients, visits peaked in December and February and were lowest in June. That's one hospital, in one climate.

It comes and goes, so the goal is keeping it calm, not making it vanish. If it lasts over a month each season, see a dermatologist.

Send this to the friend with winter flakes.
